# Method-Specific Training Configurations


## Overview
Method-Specific Training Configurations define the hyperparameters, optimization loops, and architectural adjustments required to train specific Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) variants. This family of methods solves the problem of translating theoretical NeRF formulations into stable, convergent training procedures for diverse datasets and hardware constraints. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Training Loop Setup](1522-training-loop-setup.md) and [Learning Rate Scheduling](2701-learning-rate-scheduling.md) by providing the concrete numerical values, loss functions, and network structures unique to each variant (e.g., NeRF, Mip-NeRF, DONeRF), rather than generic procedural steps.

## Shared principles
The children in this family share the fundamental goal of minimizing the photometric error between rendered images and ground truth inputs via gradient descent. All methods utilize differentiable volume rendering to compute gradients with respect to the neural network parameters. Common structural elements include the use of Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to map spatial coordinates and viewing directions to density and color, and the use of ray sampling strategies to query these networks. However, the specific activation functions, sampling densities, loss formulations, and optimizer settings vary significantly to address artifacts like aliasing, dark pixels, or memory constraints.

## Subtopics

### [NeRF Hyperparameters](3065-nerf-hyperparameters.md)
The baseline configuration for the original NeRF architecture. It uses a coarse-to-fine hierarchical sampling strategy with uniform sampling for the coarse network and importance sampling for the fine network. It employs standard MSE loss and Adam optimization with exponential learning rate decay. It is chosen when implementing the standard NeRF baseline for synthetic datasets.

### [Mip-NeRF Optimization and Activation Details](3409-mip-nerf-optimization-and-activation-details.md)
Optimization details for Mip-NeRF and JaxNeRF, focusing on stability. It distinguishes itself by removing identity concatenation from the MLP input, using a shifted softplus for density (to prevent catastrophic gradient vanishing) and a widened sigmoid for color (to prevent saturation on black/white pixels). It uses a specific warmup learning rate schedule. It is chosen to train Mip-NeRF variants robustly.

### [DONeRF](4461-donerf.md)
A training configuration that replaces standard raymarching with a dual-network architecture: a depth oracle network and a shading network. The oracle predicts optimal sample locations via classification, allowing the shading network to render with only 2–16 samples per ray. It decouples geometry estimation from appearance modeling. It is chosen when computational cost is prohibitive and depth information (or a proxy) is available or can be estimated.

### [AR-NeRF Training Configuration](12407-ar-nerf-training-configuration.md)
An unsupervised configuration for learning depth and defocus from natural images without explicit annotations. It integrates aperture rendering into the NeRF framework and uses a GAN-based regularization scheme derived from pi-GAN. It distinguishes itself by modeling camera aperture to synthesize defocused images. It is chosen for novel view synthesis with realistic depth-of-field effects from unposed natural images.

### [NeRF-SR Training Configuration](15560-nerf-sr-training-configuration.md)
A configuration for synthesizing high-resolution (HR) novel views from low-resolution (LR) inputs. It distinguishes itself by employing a supersampling strategy that renders at the target HR resolution during training, leveraging 3D consistency to generate plausible HR details without external HR ground truth. It is chosen for super-resolution tasks where only LR training data is available.

### [DP-based Configuration Selector](15955-dp-based-configuration-selector.md)
A method for selecting optimal NeRF configurations (geometry and texture parameters) for multiple segmented objects under a strict memory constraint $H$. It formulates the problem as a Multiple-Choice Knapsack (MCK) problem and uses dynamic programming to guarantee an optimal solution. It is chosen for mobile deployment where memory limits are critical.

### Blender Dataset Simplified Configuration
A simplified training setup for the Blender dataset, designed for speed rather than maximum accuracy. It uses one round of sampling, 128 samples for the proposal MLP, and 32 samples for the NeRF MLP. The proposal MLP has 4 layers and 256 hidden units, while the NeRF MLP has 8 layers and 256 (or 512) hidden units. It uses axis-aligned Integrated Positional Encoding (IPE), MSE loss, and disables the distortion regularizer [S1].

### LLFF Training Configuration
A configuration for the LLFF dataset that adapts the Mip-NeRF framework. It differs from the Blender configuration by keeping the distortion regularizer enabled and using Charbonnier loss instead of MSE. On the LLFF dataset with 256 hidden units, Mip-NeRF achieves PSNR 26.93, SSIM 0.830, LPIPS 0.177, Time 2.48 hrs, Params 0.61M. The variant "Our Model" achieves PSNR 26.68, SSIM 0.847, LPIPS 0.150, Time 2.39 hrs, Params 0.84M. With 512 hidden units, Mip-NeRF achieves PSNR 27.01, SSIM 0.845, LPIPS 0.148, Time 6.15 hrs, Params 2.27M, while "Our Model" achieves PSNR 26.86, SSIM 0.858, LPIPS 0.128, Time 3.84 hrs, Params 3.23M. The variant does not outperform Mip-NeRF in PSNR but yields improved SSIM and LPIPS metrics and a significant speedup when the NeRF MLP is large [S1].

### NeUDF Training Configuration
A configuration for training Neural Unsigned Distance Fields. It uses the ADAM optimizer with a learning rate that warms up to $2 \times 10^{-4}$ in the first 5k iterations and decreases to $1 \times 10^{-5}$ by the end. The batch size is 512 random rays sampled from 8 randomly selected camera poses per iteration. Training lasts 400k iterations, taking 9 hours with a mask and 11 hours without a mask on a single Nvidia 3090 GPU [S2].

### NeRF-SDP Training Configuration
A configuration for NeRF-SDP, which uses a Res-UNet and other components. It uses the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of $1 \times 10^{-3}$ for the Res-UNet and $5 \times 10^{-4}$ for other parts. The batch size is 500. Training runs for 250,000 steps on an Nvidia GeForce RTX 3090. The first 170,000 steps optimize auxiliary and rendering losses jointly, while the last 80,000 steps optimize only the rendering loss. Feature dimensions are 24 for 2D features and 8 for 3D features. Datasets include LLFF, IBRNet, and Google Scanned [S3].

### Neuralangelo Training Configuration
A configuration for high-fidelity neural surface reconstruction using SDFs. It samples pixels randomly without tracking statistics, using long training iterations (500k) to reduce stochasticity. The ROI is assumed to be inside a unit sphere. Inactive hash resolutions have feature vectors set to zero. The learning rate is $1 \times 10^{-3}$ with a linear warmup of 5k iterations, decaying by a factor of 10 at 300k and 400k iterations. It uses AdamW with weight decay $10^{-2}$ and $w_{iek} = 0.1$. The SDF MLP has one layer, and the color MLP has four layers. Batch size is 1 for DTU and 16 for Tanks and Temples [S4].

### GO-NeRF Training Configuration
A configuration for generating objects in NeRFs. The generation model is optimized on a single Nvidia 3090 GPU for 20,000 iterations, with 30% of iterations trained with background augmentation. The scheduler values for $\lambda_S$ and $\lambda_O$ range from 30 to 300, and $\lambda_R$ is set to 500 [S5].

### Tri-MipRF Training Configuration
A configuration for Tri-MipRF, which uses a tri-mip representation. The base mipmap shape $M_{l0}$ is $H=512, W=512, C=16$. It uses the AdamW optimizer with weight decay $1 \times 10^{-5}$ and learning rate $2 \times 10^{-3}$, scheduled by MultiStepLR. The learning rate for the Tri-Mip encoding is scaled up 10x relative to the MLP. It uses an area loss $L_{area}$, scaling pixel loss by the footprint area. Implementation uses PyTorch, tiny-cuda-nn, and nvdiffrast [S6].

### NeRF† Implementation Configuration
A variant of nerfacto using a standard MLP density field instead of HashMLPDensityField. For the Blender dataset, near/far thresholds are $t_n=2.0, t_f=6.0$. Camera optimizer, appearance embedding, distortion loss, and scene contraction are disabled. Background color is white. Batch size is 2048 rays, initial sampler is uniform, and training is 16.5k epochs. For LLFF, camera optimizer, appearance embedding, and distortion loss are disabled. Scene contraction uses $\ell_\infty$ norm. Batch size is 1024 rays during training and 2048 during evaluation. Training is 30k epochs. For leaves scenes, uniform initial proposal sampler is used. On Mip-NeRF 360, nerfacto† achieves PSNR 24.20, SSIM 0.726, LPIPS 0.247. It achieves comparable metrics to nerfacto but is significantly slower [S7].

### DVGO Reference Architecture
A reference architecture for DVGO. It uses Re:NeRF for compression. Experiments are performed on an NVIDIA A40 GPU using PyTorch 1.12 [S8].

### Nerfacto Training Configuration
The production NeRF baseline. It uses the Adam optimizer with a learning rate schedule of $10^{-2} \to 10^{-4}$, trained for 30k iterations by default [S9, unofficial].

### StyleNeRF Training Configuration
A configuration for StyleNeRF, based on the official PyTorch implementation of StyleGAN2-ADA. It uses a minibatch size of 64. Models are trained on 8 Tesla V100 GPUs for about three days, going through 25,000 images [S10, unofficial].

## Background
The original NeRF paper [S1] established the baseline training configuration, which has been adapted for various datasets (Blender, LLFF) and variants (Mip-NeRF, DONeRF, etc.). Subsequent works introduced specific optimizations to address issues like aliasing (Mip-NeRF), computational cost (DONeRF), defocus (AR-NeRF), and memory constraints (DP-based Selector). The field has evolved from simple MLP-based NeRFs to more complex architectures involving hash encodings (Instant-NGP, Neuralangelo) and GAN-based frameworks (StyleNeRF, AR-NeRF), each requiring tailored training configurations.
